method: FAO-56 single crop coefficient, constant root depth (ADR-0015)
primary_source: Allen et al. 1998, FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 (Crop evapotranspiration)

crops.stage_length_basis: FAO-56 Table 11, row 'Barley/Oats/Wheat', planting November, region Central India (total 120 days)

sources.kc: FAO-56 Table 12, group 'i. Cereals' header (Kc ini 0.3) and row 'Spring Wheat' (Kc mid 1.15, Kc end 0.25-0.4, footnote 10); read 2026-10-06 from https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e0b.htm
sources.stage_days: FAO-56 Table 11, row 'Barley/Oats/Wheat', November, Central India: 15/25/50/30, total 120; read 2026-10-06 from https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e0b.htm
sources.root_depth_m: FAO-56 Table 22, row 'Spring Wheat', maximum root depth 1.0-1.5 m; read 2026-10-06 from https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e0e.htm
sources.p: FAO-56 Table 22, row 'Spring Wheat', depletion fraction p 0.55 (for ETc about 5 mm/day); read 2026-10-06 from https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e0e.htm

crops.notes: Values transcribed from the FAO-56 HTML pages on 2026-10-06. Judgements, none confirmed with a KVK or agronomist: (1) Kc row is 'Spring Wheat', not 'Winter Wheat', to stay consistent with the 120-day Table 11 row (Table 11 winter wheat rows are 180-335 days). The Spring Wheat Kc ini cell is blank, so the Cereals group value 0.3 is used; the 'Winter Wheat, non-frozen soils' row gives 0.7. (2) Kc end 0.4 is the upper end of 0.25-0.4: Table 12 footnote 10 says the higher value is for hand-harvested crops. (3) The Table 11 row is a combined Barley/Oats/Wheat row for Central India; a farm in north-west India may fit another row. (4) Root depth 1.0 m is the lower end of 1.0-1.5; Table 22 footnote 1 says the smaller values may be used for irrigation scheduling. Limits of v1: Kc ini is the Table 12 general value (footnote 1: it rises with frequent wetting); Kc mid and Kc end are not adjusted for climate; p is not corrected for ETc other than 5 mm/day (Table 22 footnote 2).
Unfilled. Use the field/grain maize row, not sweet corn. See data/crop_water/README.md.

sources.theta: FAO-56 Table 19 'Typical soil water characteristics for different soil types', row 'Loam': theta FC 0.20-0.30, theta WP 0.07-0.17, (theta FC - theta WP) 0.13-0.18 m3/m3; read 2026-10-06 from https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e0c.htm (Chapter 7)

soils.notes: Farmer's word: domat. Values transcribed from FAO-56 Table 19 on 2026-10-06. Rule (FILL-CHECKLIST-demo.md): theta_fc - theta_wp must equal the low end of the table's (theta FC - theta WP) column, 0.13, so the alert comes earlier. Pair chosen: the midpoints of the two ranges, 0.25 and 0.12, whose difference is exactly 0.13; both lie inside their own ranges. Judgement not confirmed with a KVK or agronomist: 'domat' is mapped to the USDA class Loam.
